thesis: For the family dx/dt = x−x³+y, dy/dt = −ky, k>0, every nonempty persistent coordinate-clamp endpoint map, the specified baseline trajectory, and the qualitative equilibrium catalogues agree. Nevertheless, simultaneous release from (−1/2,1) has opposite stable endpoints for k=0.01 and k=100. Given the additional assumption that this functional family is correct, releasing x first and retaining y=1 for one time unit guarantees the positive endpoint for every k>0; the reverse order retains endpoint disagreement for every fixed finite waiting time.
claimed_contribution: The strongest defensible contribution is the combination of an explicit nonidentification construction with a contrasting control guarantee inside the same family. The manuscript distinguishes representing an outcome from identifying it, and identifying one procedure's outcome from finding another procedure that succeeds uniformly. It expressly disclaims priority and does not claim that its control guarantee follows from endpoint evidence alone.

findings.manuscript_location: Systems and evidence: “Numerical eigenvalues and relaxation rates are not included in this qualitative evidence”; The question and its scope; Bibliography.
findings.claim: The literature discussion omits a close predecessor for the mechanism by which equilibrium interventions conceal relative rates.
findings.analysis: Bongers, Blom and Mooij compare X = BX − X′ + ΓE with X = BX − ΛX′ + ΓE, where Λ is invertible and diagonal. Their equilibrium models and qualifying intervened equilibria coincide. This closely anticipates the hidden-rate mechanism, although convergence is separately qualified. See [§4.6, Example 4.21 and the following paragraph](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.m.mooij/articles/1803.08784v4.pdf#page=36). The demonstrated omission concerns literature positioning; it does not establish prior publication of V06's opposite release endpoints.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The contribution cannot reasonably be framed as discovering that intervention equilibria can conceal dynamical rates. The stronger claim about identical initial-state-sensitive clamp outcomes and different released attractors remains distinct in the inspected literature.
findings.repair_conditions: Discuss this predecessor and distinguish equality of equilibrium equations from V06's proved convergence and equality of the entire stipulated endpoint evidence.

findings.manuscript_location: An application: choosing the order of withdrawal: “The successful procedure uses no additional measurements to estimate k” and “Identification of an unknown parameter, identification of one procedure’s outcome, and successful choice among procedures are different tasks.”
findings.claim: The control application needs comparison with existing results on temporary switching under parameter uncertainty.
findings.analysis: Sootla and colleagues already formulate lasting switching by finite pulses and bound switching sets under uncertain parameters; see [§2.1 and Corollary 9](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/191987/1/border_final.pdf#page=6). Sootla and Ernst explicitly seek a pulse succeeding throughout a parameter interval in [§IV, Problem 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1708.00232#page=5). Thus successful temporary control without exact parameter identification is established. Neither inspected result supplies V06's exhaustive-evidence equivalence and reverse-order impossibility.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Any broad novelty interpretation of control despite parameter uncertainty must narrow. The specific withdrawal-order contrast, including the guarantee over all k>0, is not displaced by these comparisons.
findings.repair_conditions: Locate the application within robust pulse-control research and specify that the proposed contribution is its connection to the displayed nonidentification example and withdrawal order.

findings.manuscript_location: The question and its scope: “the available account of Ryan and Dablander rests on publisher excerpts, not full-text access”; Bibliography, Ryan and Dablander 2025.
findings.claim: The Ryan–Dablander attribution remains only partly independently verified.
findings.analysis: The authors' publication record confirms the paper's existence, authorship, title, year and journal. Publisher full-text, abstract and PDF requests failed; repository attempts also yielded no readable article. Search excerpts resemble the manuscript's pulse/press description, but I did not treat them as primary-text verification. The manuscript accurately discloses this limitation.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: No inaccurate attribution has been demonstrated. The specific §1/Appendix A attribution remains unverified from an opened primary text; the self-contained mathematical conclusions do not depend on it.
findings.repair_conditions: Inspect an accessible article copy before removing the qualification, and confirm the relevant section locations and the scope of its intervention definitions.

surviving_contribution: The inspected predecessors leave a specific remainder: a smooth two-variable family with identical endpoint maps for every nonempty constant coordinate clamp and every free initial state, identical stated baseline and qualitative stability evidence, but opposite stable endpoints after the same simultaneous release. The same construction then separates that unidentified procedure from a uniformly successful staged withdrawal, while proving that every fixed finite delay in the reverse order preserves disagreement. This is more specific than loss of dynamical information at equilibrium, the holding/releasing distinction, or robust temporary control considered separately. I did not locate this exact combination in the primary passages inspected. That establishes a distinct remainder within this search, not exhaustive originality.
remaining_questions: Does an earlier source establish the same initial-state-sensitive equivalence across all nonempty coordinate clamps together with different released attractors? No such result was located in the opened texts.

In An application: choosing the order of withdrawal, the guarantee holds “for every k>0.” Whether this particular hybrid clamp procedure follows directly from an existing robust-control theorem, rather than requiring a small extension of its assumptions, was not established.
limitations: The complete supplied manuscript and bibliography were read. External sources were examined at the locations recorded below; opening a PDF is not represented as reading every page.
This was a finite public-web search across causal equilibrium models, dynamical identification, pulse control, and temporary network control. It does not establish an exhaustive priority result.
Ryan and Dablander's article was not readable through the available web routes. Search excerpts were used to locate evidence, not to establish its argument.
The sequential Boolean-control paper at the CMSB20 URL repeatedly timed out. Its search description was not used to establish substantive overlap.

This is a literature and citation audit, not an independent numerical or comprehensive formal-proof certification. The manuscript's displayed construction is self-contained and makes no claim that its equations or estimates are quoted from a predecessor.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Substantive overlap in relative-rate changes concealed by intervened equilibrium equations.
closest_predecessors.difference: The linear construction does not establish V06's multistable endpoint split or equality of all initial-state-sensitive clamp outcome maps.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: V06 turns hidden dynamics into a proved difference between stable release endpoints while matching its stronger evidence specification.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: [§4.6, Example 4.21 and convergence qualification, PDF pp. 36–37](https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.m.mooij/articles/1803.08784v4.pdf#page=36).

closest_predecessors.overlap: Substantive overlap in finite-duration control that produces a lasting switch despite parameter uncertainty.
closest_predecessors.difference: Corollary 9 uses a compact parameter set and bounding-system assumptions; it does not analyze V06's clamp-equivalent family or opposing withdrawal orders.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The connection between nonidentification and the particular uniform withdrawal guarantee remains.

closest_predecessors.overlap: A successful pulse can be selected for every parameter value in a specified interval without identifying the exact parameter.
closest_predecessors.difference: The analysis uses monotonicity and model-derived functions; it does not infer release outcomes from exhaustive constant-clamp endpoints.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: V06's all-k withdrawal-order theorem and its pairing with indistinguishable evidence are not established here.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Direct conceptual overlap: removing a constraint is an action whose consequences a holding model may not represent.
closest_predecessors.difference: The piston argument compares model adequacy and causal relationships under different constraints; it does not construct two smooth systems agreeing on V06's exhaustive evidence.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: V06 supplies a precise evidence-relative nonidentification result and a separate withdrawal-order guarantee.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Direct formal background for initial-condition-sensitive equilibrium outcome maps.
closest_predecessors.difference: Theorem 2 constructs a representation using all intervention targets, including the empty target; it does not identify the omitted map from nonempty-target maps.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: V06 demonstrates this inferential gap in a concrete family. It is compatible with, rather than a counterexample to, the representation theorem.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Substantive application overlap: an intervention effective while maintained may fail after withdrawal, and temporary control can secure an enduring attractor.
closest_predecessors.difference: The inspected analysis uses specified network dynamics and intervention tests, not two smooth systems indistinguishable under every persistent coordinate clamp.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: V06's evidence-identification claim and exact order-dependent guarantees remain separate.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: [Stable-motif blocking discussion and transient-intervention validation](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004193), particularly retrieved lines 221–226 and 260–265.

citation_audit.evidence: Theorem 2's proof constructs a constraint for every target subset; §1.1 explicitly identifies the null intervention. The [official record](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v115/blom20a.html) and [volume record](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v115/) confirm authors, title, PMLR 115, publication in 2020 and the 2019 conference. The manuscript correctly separates representation from inference.

The [official proceedings record](https://proceedings.mlr.press/r5/dash05a.html) confirms the bibliographic identity. The manuscript does not misattribute its stronger release theorem to Dash.

Publisher search excerpts are consistent with the description but are insufficient for verification under this audit's standard.
